OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must contain 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. Stored and returned in E.164 form (e.g. '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag. When true, allows creating this owner even if an
            existing owner has the same lastName and address (compared
            case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace); otherwise such a
            request is rejected with 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where
                LAST3 is the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and
                NNNN is a global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more
                than the number of owners at the time the owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content

The refactor is complete and verified. Compilation succeeds (tests ran), and the test result is **identical to the baseline**: the same single pre-existing failure — `AcceptanceTest` NPEs at line 21 because `householdId` isn't returned yet, which is expected since I did **not** implement the feature. ## What I did

I prepared the ground for the upcoming `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` change without implementing it. The household concept was previously a one-shot boolean check (`isHouseholdDuplicate`) buried in the controller — a shape that would force the change to bolt on ad-hoc `assignHousehold` / `householdId` helpers and cram more branching into `addOwner`. I moved it to where the change will naturally land:

**`Owner.java`** — gave household *identity* a home on the entity, alongside its other domain helpers (`getPet`, `addPet`):
- Added `sameHouseholdAs(Owner other)` — encapsulates the "same last name + address" rule.
- Moved the `normalize` helper here as a private static.

This is exactly where `getHouseholdId`/`setHouseholdId` will sit, so the change concentrates household state and behavior in one class.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — reshaped the detection into the seam the change needs:
- Replaced `isHouseholdDuplicate(Owner): boolean` with `findHouseholdMember(Owner): Optional<Owner>`, which *returns the existing household member* rather than just a yes/no. That member is precisely what the change must grab to share a stable `householdId` with.
- The existing 409-conflict guard now reads `findHouseholdMember(owner).isPresent()` — behavior identical.
- Removed the now-redundant `normalize` (moved to `Owner`); added the `Optional` import.

**Behavior preservation:** every existing code path is byte-for-byte equivalent — same normalization, same matching rule, same 409 semantics. The refactor is purely structural.

Note on the one failing test: `AcceptanceTest.coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` targets the *unimplemented* feature (it reads back `householdId`), so it fails today and still fails after my change — as it must, since the brief says not to implement the change yet. There are no other tests, and nothing that passed before regressed.
